t:
(a) The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, may carry out a program to distribute surplus dental and medical equipment of the Department of Defense, at no cost to the Department of Defense, to Indian Health Service facilities and to federally-qualified health centers (within the meaning of section 1905(l)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396d(l)(2)(B))). 
    (b) In carrying out this provision, the Secretary of Defense shall give the Indian Health Service a property disposal priority equal to the priority given to the Department of Defense and its twelve special screening programs in distribution of surplus dental and medical supplies and equipment.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in coordination with" signals participation, but the coordination is between two federal cabinet secretaries, which stays inside the federal government. The Indian Health Service is a federal agency, and federally-qualified health centers are only recipients of surplus equipment, not parties consulted before a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is provided.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, may carry out a program to distribute surplus dental and medical equipment of the Department of Defense

qwen_block.w: The section describes coordination between two federal cabinet secretaries (Defense and Health and Human Services). Both are inside the federal government. The recipients of the equipment (Indian Health Service and federally-qualified health centers) are not involved in the decision-making process or consultation; they are merely recipients of a distribution program. Therefore, there is no participation by outside parties in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, may carry out a program to distribute surplus dental and medical equipment of the Department of Defense

opus.w: The only coordination is between two federal cabinet secretaries, which is coordination inside the government and not participation. The Indian Health Service is a federal agency. The federally-qualified health centers only receive the surplus equipment, which is like receiving a benefit; they are not consulted before any federal decision. No hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, may carry out a program to distribute surplus dental and medical equipment
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "in coordination with" counts as participation. It doesn't, because both parties (the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Health and Human Services) are federal officials. The health centers and Indian Health Service facilities only receive surplus equipment; they have no role in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a distribution program involving coordination between two federal agencies (Defense and Health and Human Services). Since both actors are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. The recipients are beneficiaries of the distribution, not participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, may carry out a program to distribute surplus dental and medical equipment
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "coordination" with the Secretary of Health and Human Services constitutes participation. However, both the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Health and Human Services are federal officials inside the government. Intra-governmental coordination is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. The recipients (Indian Health Service facilities and federally-qualified health centers) are recipients of a distribution program, not participants in a decision-making process like an advisory board or consultation prior to a rule.
